cards.explanation: The answer is an angel. Luke 2:21 says Jesus was given "…the name the angel had given Him before He was conceived." The name was settled long before anybody could pack a diaper bag, friends. I got my name carved into a handle, but His was handed down from heaven first.

The answer is Jerusalem. Luke 2:22 says His parents "…brought Him to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord…" That's the trip, and it has a destination. Good thing too, bakers, because nobody wants a family road trip with no destination.

The answer is to offer a sacrifice. Luke 2:24 says they came "…to offer the sacrifice specified in the Law of the Lord…" The Law named the offering too: "A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons." So the visit had two jobs, friends: presenting the Child and bringing the offering.

The answer is True. Luke 2:26 says the Holy Spirit had revealed to Simeon that "…he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ." That's a promise he carried around, friends. Imagine knowing the answer is coming and still having to wait for it.

The answer is False. Luke 2:27 says, "Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple courts." The Spirit led him in, and Mary and Joseph brought in the child Jesus right then. If that's chance, friends, then I'm just a stamper who got called out of a junk drawer by accident.

The answer is that his eyes have seen God's salvation. Simeon says it right there: "For my eyes have seen Your salvation…" He had been told he'd see the Lord's Christ (Luke 2:26), and now he was holding the Child. So he's at peace and ready to be dismissed, friends.

The answer is all people. Simeon says God prepared this salvation "…in the sight of all people…" That's a big, wide-open view, bakers. It isn't tucked away in a corner of the temple, and it isn't meant for just a few.

The answer is Gentiles. Simeon calls the salvation "…a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to Your people Israel." The Gentiles are the nations outside Israel. So the light shines on them and brings glory to Israel too, friends.

The answer is the rise and fall of many. Simeon, the righteous man in the temple, tells Mary the Child "…is appointed to cause the rise and fall of many in Israel…" That's a weighty word to give a mother, friends. I think she was holding a lot in that moment.
The answer is False. Simeon says the Child will "…be a sign that will be spoken against…" So not everyone will speak well of Him, friends. It's a heavy word for Mary, and I think it landed hard.
The answer is hearts. Simeon says it happens "…so that the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed…" It's about what's inside people, bakers. The Child brings that out into the open.

The answer is that she never leaves the temple. Luke 2:37 says Anna "…never left the temple, but worshiped night and day, fasting and praying." Her address was the temple, friends. Mine was a junk drawer, and I had no choice about it.

The answer is that she gives thanks to God. Luke 2:38 says Anna "…gave thanks to God…" She came forward at that moment and did it, friends. Then she spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.

The answer is everyone waiting for Jerusalem's redemption. Luke 2:38 says Anna "…spoke about the Child to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem." She told everyone who was waiting, bakers. Anna isn't keeping this one to herself.

The answer is Nazareth in Galilee. Luke 2:39 says they returned "…to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth." Nazareth is home, friends. They went back once they had done everything required by the Law of the Lord.

The answer is True. Luke 2:40 says, "He was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him." The Child grew and became strong, and that's how Luke ends this part of the story, friends. A good note to end on.
